reviews.text: 游戏画面风格是那种复古载具射击的感觉，打起来有老式街机射击游戏的手感。 玩法核心循环就是：出门拆房子捡破烂，搬材料回来盖基地升级各种功能，然后守家扛住一波波怪，最后推掉敌人基地通关。 这游戏节奏还算适中，适合喜欢“打怪+盖家”循环的玩家
游戏核心是收集资源何塔防，你将驾驶小坦克通过破坏建筑物来搜集资源，将资源用以建造你的基地与防线，比传统塔防更有趣味性，游戏很考验建筑的摆放布局，合理的摆放能够事半功倍，同时你也可以主动出击，重创敌人基地。

浅浅玩了一下子，还挺有意思的，玩家将作为一位再修复者建设岛屿，然而建设岛屿需要物资，物资怎么来呢，当然就是快乐的到处拆拆拆捡回来啦(偶尔也会捡到人，什么，那是你的家？抱歉，我只是觉得俺的基地比你的家更宜居.jpg)，获取到足够的材料后修建足够稳固的防御工事(推荐使用建筑中有路的那个方向与其他建筑连接，会获得强化效果)来抵挡敌人的进攻 没想到整个游戏只有两个人参与，目前体验不错，这风格还挺有那味的，就是个人比较习惯鼠标点击过剧情对话，如果能加上就好了，期待后续更新 对了，进游戏最好先改下帧率限制，默认无限制还是有点吃性能了
这款小游戏性价比直接拉满，清新柔和的卡通美术风格观感舒适，坦克驾驶操控调校得十分到位，灵活顺滑没有笨重拖沓感。自建建筑布局合理，不会遮挡行进路线，游玩体验十分流畅。游戏优化表现出色，运行稳定无卡顿。融合塔防、射击与基建多重玩法，驾驶坦克清理废墟搜集物资，搭建庇护基地营救幸存人员，玩法丰富有层次，沉浸感十足越玩越上瘾。

Existential Treads by is a great casual game. It looks and sounds great, lots of splashy effects, full of action, and very easy to just pick up and jump straight into. Destroy ruins to gather resources, build defences, soup up your tank, and try to reclaim the land by hunting down enemy towers between waves of attacks before you're overcome. Gets hectic! [h1]废土履迹 简评[/h1] 很爽快的带点肉鸽元素的建造＋射击游戏。游戏玩法听起来成分复杂，实际游玩体验下来还是相当不错的，游戏世界设定中，人类文明被ai毁灭，而我们扮演的炮台是恢复文明的希望 游戏玩法上，我们通过射击周围碍事的建筑来获得各种材料，材料数量满足任务就可以在在基地周围选择建几种不同的建筑，建筑功能不同，比如帮我们抵抗攻击，提高我们移动速度，与其他建筑连接起来会提升效率等等 而每过一段时间就会有敌人从噪音塔中出来攻击我们的基地，基地血量清空我们就失败，我们可以通过多种手段抵抗，陷阱，路障，生产的特殊子弹，炸弹等等 游戏难度算不上低，每摧毁一座塔后续敌人的入侵强度就更高，而我们的生命也只会在草地恢复，，我们最多只能死亡两次，要不然也是失败 总的来说游戏难度比较高，考验策略性，射击手感很舒服，操作很舒服，且卡通同的画风相当魔性，喜欢俯视角射击游戏和建造游戏甚至是塔防的都推荐尝试一下，几种玩法结合起来很好玩 [quote]关注&加入∶[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45540934/admin/reviews_manage/]深澜探索者[/url][/quote]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44181848/] 【更多适合Steam Deck的好游戏推荐，请关注GPD掌机鉴赏家！】[/url] 很有意思的小品级游戏，把“开车拆家”和“塔防”结合得挺巧妙。开着坦克在城市废墟里兜风，把碍事的破房子轰倒搜刮资源，再回来规划基地布局，这个循环非常解压。 特别好评的是手柄适配做得极好，在Steam Deck或掌机上玩简直是绝配，摇杆走位和瞄准的手感甚至比键鼠还跟手，躺着玩几个小时都不累。战斗那种复古街机的爽快感一下就出来了。 不过实话实说，这游戏实在太短了。几个多小时就通关了，内容量不大，通关后重开的价值不高。后期建筑多了偶尔会掉帧，优化还能再打磨下。 总的来说，如果你只是想找个周末下午打发时间，这游戏绝对爽快；但如果你追求长流程和高重复可玩性，可能会觉得有点意犹未尽。

Unbalanced mess.

首先无脑入没什么问题 当前还没到给好评，主要有2个点 1 地图的扩张机制，因为建造是基于草地，草地是基于清空垃圾建筑 也就是，清空垃圾建筑，扩展草地，草地上建造自己的东西，大概这个逻辑。 所以草地变得极其重要，目前游戏中，草地的扩张逻辑不是很合理，比较慢，其次，你不知道为什么他到这个点，不往外扩展了，好几次周围没什么垃圾建筑了，但是就是不扩展了。所以这个扩展逻辑，我作为一个玩家，通了几关还是完全不清楚机制是什么 2 建筑的连接逻辑 建造的东西，很多不知道哪里是口，可以和其他建筑连接，并且无法重新调整位置，旋转等等，那么一不小心造错了，就很蛋疼。 那么造成了你建造的时候，就要预先设想到口朝哪里，然后怎么连接下一个建筑 但是，建造又是基于草地的扩展，换句话说，草地没扩展到那个地方，我有一个明明可以连的建筑，也无法连接 所以1和2两个问题叠加起来的时候，简直无语。 还有一个小点可以优化，没有塔楼的时候，不要出塔楼加强的相关建筑，不然造了也是白造。我一开始以为塔楼只是 优化了以上问题，会给好评，游戏本身可以，价格也合适，无脑可以入，但是这2个点在我看来是非常核心的机制问题，所以改之前会先挂差评

建议打五折时购买。 以首发版本来讲，这是一款合格的小游戏，完整体验该游戏也仅需3小时。不过，它的通关思路比较单一，且没有BOSS敌人可打，因此每一关的实际难度并不高，难度曲线非常平缓，导致该游戏的可重复游玩性偏低，我认为这是作者目前要考虑的方向。 我希望作者在未来版本能够加入多人联机模式，并且新增多种通关目标，比如限时防御，BOSS战等，这样能够大幅提升游戏性和可重复游玩性。

《废土履迹》是一款废土风塔防游戏，将玩家开车收集资源和选择建筑工事的方式相结合，拉高游戏的自由度，从而获得更多的乐趣。游戏很容易上手，不同的建筑之间会有连携作用，满足一定的条件也会解锁额外的加成奖励，如果所有排布都能完成这种要求那么整局游戏体验就会特别爽快。 [h2]游戏玩法 [/h2] 玩家主控的是一个小车，可以攻击周围的废弃建筑从而获得资源，家里的居民会自动过来搬资源运回基地，如果有建筑工事正在建造，会自动消耗这些资源。小车遇到落单的居民还可以让他们上车，运回基地就会增加人口，方便做更多的建筑。当然，最后的目的是击毁敌方老巢，不过老巢数量不止一个，还有守塔水晶的作用，一定要避开它们发射的攻击。 建造方面会随机出现三个选项，根据自己己方基地的状态进行铺设。防御塔肯定要在最外层，起到一个保护作用。民居可以和很多建筑结合产生额外作用，而且也能提高居民上限，也是重中之重。其余的维修房、炮弹房等建筑属于功能性的，随着关卡的深入越来越有用，但是位置一定要往中间放，不能太靠近外圈。运气不好的时候可能防御塔没那么多，只能由我们小炮车顶上，不过我们的火力也不弱。也可以设计陷阱进行布防，不过要注意烟花陷阱基本没用，出怪都是分散开来冲击的，烟花陷阱不适合防御，只能浪费一次机会。 游戏的玩法其实还好，内容不多，对于目前这个价格来说4~5小时的流程其实还可以。不过建筑选择方面带有强烈的随机要素，有时候一局下来可能抽不到几个要用的建筑，这样打起来就难多了。而且前期的武器到后面也派不上用场了，要多搞有着大范围伤害的炮台，能坚持更久。 总体来说，《废土履迹》的体验还不错，玩起来确实也挺爽，塔防方面也比较有深度。不过一些游戏设计方面的体验还是需要改进一下，才能让玩家玩的更舒服。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~

RNG. Games need to stop being so dependent on RNG to be a main focus in games. Can you win with the RNG? Yes. Can you win every scenario with RNG? No. There HAS to be some sort of luck. Get lucky and get the things you need to succeed. Just because the very beginning is possible with any bad RNG doesn't give games a pass to be dependent on RNG later. Why can't I choose what I want? What's so unreasonable about that? If the game feels too cheap to sell without the RNG that gives the game replay-ability then reduce the cost.

How often do we get a solid shooter, tower defense, city builder and a marvelous indie game all into one?!?!! Who knows, but you might want to help and build up this settlement. We got plenty of a NOISE-y neighbors to deal with first! o0o Game-play : 10/10 Game is a very simple premise. Build up your city, create defense towers, diversify on how you build up your city to give you certain upgrades/benefits and defend yourself against the oncoming hordes of NOISE (the game's enemies). The game features some clever touches here from not just how quick you feel in the battlefield, but even the way it shows where attacks are coming to better help you prepare. Most of your city building amusingly enough comes from destroying the buildings around you spread the "green" around as you expand the settlement. Graphics : 10/10 I really have to credit SO much of this indie game's dedication to detail. While it's a very cartoony fashion on the top, EVERYTHING feels polished from unique looks of the buildings, towers, abandoned city and even the resources that stick out from buildings. Oh darn, need metal to build your settlement? Hold up! There's these buildings you came across that have these defining metal pipes sticking out from them! Shoot that building down and WHOA, you got your metal! o0o There's so much to praise about good work from whether its the style and its colorful focus on your settlement, the shaky/unique look of your tank, to even the settlers how they don different hats/clothing to each their tasks that get assigned. Explosions, lighting to indicate the presence of the NOISE, it's all there. I could go on, but there was true passion poured into this game that I hope you see too. <3 Controls: 10/10 Haven't yet played a game that controls as sharp and perfect as Existential Treads. Played the game with the ole mouse/keyboard, but this game never failed for its simple controls. You didn't feel like you couldn't control your tank well enough or didn't know how to rotate buildings or flip between different weapons. As simple as pineapple on pizza. Shocking, but true. o0o Sound/Music : 10/10 Although there isn't a HUGE variety in the music, but the game utilizes the limited to stay perfect. The chipper music as you build, the ramping up as the time ticks down before the next wave and the speedy pace of the wave on the attack to make your eyes/brain panic. Despite that, you'll never tire from the game being quiet (in a good way). There's no dead zone of any sounds/music that doesn't tickle your eyes (or notify you when you're out of Boost/Gas). Even when the defining pitch you hear when the noise are directly attacking you or you can hear the sound of an enemy tower charging up its next shot. And for the love of everything, I gotta immensely praise the game's main title music. No track better sums up the energy, the rock, the fun you got in store when starting up the game. A genuine head-rocking masterpiece. Difficulty : 10/10 No joke, this game handles its difficulty so beautifully. The tower defense games can vary insanely on their toughness and worse is a game where despite your efforts (or RNG) you just CANNOT beat a level/wave. Existential Treads doesn't do that at all. You naturally scale up more and more slowly, and you gotta make sure to swing by your settlement when the wave is attacking. It can be dead simple (the additional weapons help), but I really actually enjoy how the devs were really clever to vary up how the NOISE slightly vary or creep around the attack path. So much so, that I was focusing on one side of my base and a few NOISE creeped around my HQ to give me a Game Over. The balance between a bit of hand-holding but just enough to learn how to stay on your feet. Absolutely LUV'd the game's difficulty. <3 Story : 10/10 Nothing too crazy here, but the game does off a quick tale to tell as you go about the campaign. Even how they even include added touches from the saved people you come across as a way to introduce some addtional storytelling (or the world's zany lore). Some great laughs along the way, but this game definitely keeps its humor as well as a pretty good/wholesome message by the end of it. Chalk this up as another solid win. *nods* Audience: Oh gosh, this indie game EASILY goes for everybody. Sure, lots of explosions, guns, but no actual blood/violence to be near that extreme. The cartoon-y aspect only benefits the game and I think any age could pick-up and enjoy this game. Recommended, but it needs more depth I had a fun time with this game overall. It’s colorful, has a nice Borderlands-inspired art style, and feels very welcoming from the first minute. The gameplay is incredibly simple. You don’t need a tutorial, and if you’ve played similar games before, you’ll understand everything within seconds. Performance was excellent on my MacBook Pro M4 (around 2 GB RAM usage), with smooth gameplay and no noticeable bugs. Considering this was developed by just two people, it’s a very impressive achievement. That said, there are several areas I think could be improved. Resources * Trees are everywhere, but eventually there’s almost no wood left. At that point, the only reliable source is demolishing ruins. * Grass sometimes grows very slowly. * Without the seedling ammunition, it’s difficult to make meaningful progress. Towers & Buildings * Towers are currently far too weak to make a real difference. * Tower upgrades keep appearing even when I don’t have any towers or when all tower slots are already occupied. * The building selection feels too random. Sometimes I get multiple tower upgrades despite not owning a single tower. * The game frequently offers buildings I already have enough of. For example, after building two repair stations, I rarely need a third. A smarter selection system would make progression feel much better. * The Tavern currently doesn’t seem to provide any meaningful benefit. Weapons * The weapon variety is lacking. The starting weapon feels very ineffective against enemies. * Ammo for the rapid-fire weapon is produced very slowly and only if you’ve already built the Gunsmith. * The game would benefit from more weapon variety. * Ammo hotkeys should always stay fixed (1 = Standard, 2 = Rapid Fire, 3 = Dynamite, etc.). Currently the key assignments change when one ammo type runs out, which quickly becomes frustrating. * It should also be possible to switch ammunition while firing. Overall, this is a charming and well-crafted game, but after a while it becomes very repetitive. It lacks the depth needed to keep things interesting, especially regarding weapons and the building progression system. Being able to move buildings and towers after placing them would also be a great quality-of-life improvement. Right now, towers are nice to have, but they don’t really impact the gameplay in a meaningful way. Would I recommend it? Yes. It’s a fun game for a few relaxing sessions, especially if you’re looking for something casual. With more depth and better progression, it could become something truly great.

You can repair your towers with the glue gun, and you can add houses for the city building feature for workers. Ash & Adam's Existential Treads is essentially 3 genres in one, FPS, Tower Defense and City Builder. I'm not a fan of the city building aspect. You can attack the pink towers where your monsters come out of, but 9 out of 10 times you'll take serious damage, so just scrap that idea if you don't have grass seeds to plant a defense tower close to the pink towers where the monsters exit from. Kind of an unfair disadvantage you're burdened with. This game would definitely be so much better if there were upgrades you can carry over to the next game. Unfair game, too frustrating, too many directions the monsters can attack your castle. but overall a neat concept which desperately needs roguelike abilities. Full controller support.

This is one of the best games I can't recommend out there. I love the look. The world has a grid system for item placement, but they conceal the lines of it juuuust well enough that everything looks vibrant and pleasant to look at, while keeping it obvious how much space there is between things when you're placing a building. The sound design is also great. The bomb and bullet hose sound powerful, the enemies make a threatening, characteristic chittering as they approach, the way the music changes is... Well, actually, there's this thing where it starts a guitar loop when an enemy wave appears, then starts a different invasion song when the enemies are close enough. That works really well when the enemies are close enough to your base, but it gets kinda silly when they're far away, because that build-up loop just keeps going. I also wish they had more songs. Maybe something like... whole new tracks that change with the different biomes? The problem is that there are serious balance issues, and they just spoil the whole game because it means you can be screwed by the RNG. Basically: the Gunsmith is, by far, the most powerful building in the game. Almost everything else needs a buff of some kind. In harder levels, you need to get a Gunsmith early enough just to have a chance. Getting two is much better. Also, houses take a lot of Settlers to fill, but they do barely anything for the buildings that produce special weapons, and are ridiculously powerful on other buildings, like the Repair Bay. Speaking of the Repair Bay! Sometimes I just don't get a Repair Bay or Glue Vat to fix broken buildings, or only get one when I have the option to build something even more crucial, like my first Gunsmith, so I have to risk it and wait for another one to show up, which it DOESN'T. On the other side of the coin, the Boost Battery is completely useless. It lets your tank go longer before needing a recharge, but not much longer, and the seeds from the Sower let you recharge in enemy territory by planting the grass you need, anyway. On top of that, the Tetris-shaped buildings mean that you can have a plan, with all your buildings laid out for it, but fail to get a house in the shape you need to fill things out. In theory, you can fix this by being flexible, but in practice, you get very little space to work with, especially at the start. That free building you get in the beginning? Yeah, you need to wait for the HQ to spread grass around. This is slow and random, which means you're delaying the ability of the Town Council to give you your second list of buildings if you're trying to follow an optimal plan that makes the best possible use of your limited space. Why not just give the HQ the ability to spread grass up to four tiles away, really, really fast, at the start of each level? The balance of the crew members isn't much better either. One just gives you a slight enhancement to your boost battery, which, again, is mooted by the Sower. Another one gives you extra Settler slots in your HQ, which is actually kind of a mixed blessing because it means you need more Settlers from the start. This guy would be MUCH better if you got the extra Settlers to fill those slots. It's frustrating, because the game gets some little details right. If you destroy the only Noise tower that's sending a wave, it will restart the timer rather than just switching to a different tower! If you mine out all the resources of a certain type, the game tells you! If your next building is waiting on resources of a certain type, your collectors prioritize that resource! So great!... So, how'd they mess up the BIG stuff? UPDATE: I've been playing the new mini-missions that came out as I was writing playing the campaign. One of them, Swarm, is just completely busted on the Heavy Treads version. You flat-out don't have the damage you need to destroy the tougher Noise enemies, even with Defense Towers. I was hanging in there just by running into them, sacrificing my health to clear waves. I just can't believe the devs play-tested this and thought it was okay.
